items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe and I’m off camera talking to Bob Kinkel... [INTERVIEWEE] My pleasure. Good to see you.

ctx.x: His piano and physics studies, along with an active curiosity in how things work, prepared him well for a diverse career in the music business. Bob has worked at the Record Plant, been active in session work and jingle writing, and with partners Jon Oliva and Paul O’Neill, transformed an idea for a rock opera into the phenomenally successful Trans-Siberian Orchestra.
Bob was interviewed in Clinton, New York, on October 31, 2012, by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and I’m off camera talking to Bob Kinkel, a Hamilton alum, sitting in the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. Thanks for being here.
